newsitem.title: USA: NASA delays U.S. shuttle landing.
newsitem.headline: NASA delays U.S. shuttle landing.

text.p: Flight controllers delayed space shuttle Columbia's return to earth on Thursday due to cloudy skies at its Florida landing site.
The five astronauts were 15 minutes away from firing Columbia's braking rockets to begin their descent when mission control called off the planned 7:33 a.m. EST (1233 GMT) landing.
"The clouds around KSC (Kennedy Space Center) are not going to cooperate with us on this particular attempt," mission control's Curt Brown informed the crew. "We are no-go for the deorbit burn."
Forecasters advised against a landing because clouds were moving off the Atlantic Ocean toward the shuttle's landing strip at its Florida base.
Columbia had another landing opportunity at the Kennedy Space Center at 9:10 a.m. EST (1410 GMT). The shuttle could also be diverted to NASA's backup runway at Edwards Air Force Base in California.
NASA ordered Columbia home a day early because of a poor weather outlook for both landing sites on Friday.
